at_sea: SUPERSEDES 2026-08-05-the-fourth-refusal-and-the-lines-that-learn, written earlier the same day and left standing (the door refuses an overwrite — Law 7). That slate carries two claims of mine that are now reversed; read this one. system_rackmount + harbor_master, and the seam between them. RATIFIED BY AKIEN 2026-08-04 AND BUILT, both proofs green: (1) system_rackmount grew a SECOND DOOR — ask(name, value) -> bool, the may-I door, resolving through the SAME _resolve the subscribe door uses so a pull and a push on one menu item cannot drift; it returns a VERDICT, never a reading (Law 6), proven as a TYPE because scanning a bool for the reading's digits is a check that cannot fail. (2) memory_floor mounted beside cpu_threshold and runs the OTHER direction (crossed by falling BELOW) — its first named consumer arrived, which is what edge (a) said would mount it. (3) THE SAMPLER STOPPED LYING ABOUT TIME: it served os.getloadavg()[0], a ~60s decaying average the kernel recomputes every 5s. MEASURED, 4 burners on this 8-core box: runnable went 2 -> 6 within one second while the average went 5.5% -> 9.1% and still read 15.4% twelve seconds in. Now reads /proc/loadavg field 4 + MemAvailable, both instantaneous. Verified the new tooth BITES: the old sampler rises 0.0 points where the new one rises 50.0. (4) harbor_master binds a FOURTH REFUSAL — Unresourced (authorized, proven, legal, and still refused), plus Grant.issued_at + ttl_seconds (GRANT_TTL_SECONDS = 10.0, Akien's number) and GrantExpired subclassing Unauthorized on purpose so every 'no grant' guarantee holds for 'lapsed grant', including writing no record. THE TTL AND THE METRIC ARE ONE DECISION: a grant must outlast the time a launch takes to become visible or it lapses while the next asker is blind; runnable shows a launch in under a second, the average it replaced would have needed ~60s. NOTHING COUNTS BUILDERS — the proof's fake resource owner RAISES on every door but ask (the raw reading, and every census shape), so a build that pulled a number or counted a fleet dies on a path whose happy case is identical. Commits: cairn 02d0a5a (build) and faab5bd (the learning ruling); CairnCommons ded0f01 (the note). Both pushed. HARBOR_LINES' TWO NUMBERS ARE PLACEHOLDERS. cpu 75.0 derives from Akien's measured 6-of-8 crawl point; memory 1024 is a HYPOTHESIS labelled as one in the code (Law 3) — nobody has measured what a builder needs to not thrash. And the learning method that will replace them has THREE terms, not two: baseline, marginal cost, and a RESERVE (the headroom the host keeps for itself) — ceiling = (usable - baseline) / marginal.

AN ASSUMPTION HIDES INSIDE THE 75: it encodes 'one builder costs one runnable'. Akien's worked example (corrected by him 2026-08-05: baseline 20%, +10 POINTS per builder, 6 -> 80%, rest kept as headroom) is CONSISTENT with that assumption — ~0.8 runnable per builder on 8 cores — not evidence for it. Unmeasured; the measurement decides.
